why: Pain is real and protective, but its intensity is not a precise measure of tissue damage.

slides.title: Pain Has a Protective Purpose
slides.content: Pain is a real experience designed to protect you. It can be influenced by information from your body as well as context, expectations, past experiences, sleep, stress, and perceived safety.

slides.title: Pain and Damage Are Not the Same
slides.content: Pain can occur with tissue injury, but the amount of pain does not precisely reveal the amount of damage. This does not make pain imaginary.

slides.title: Context Can Turn Protection Up
slides.content: Uncertainty, fear, poor sleep, stress, or a previous difficult experience can increase concern and sensitivity. These are influences—not proof of one cause.

slides.title: Confidence Can Change the Experience
slides.content: Clear information, support, a manageable plan, and successful movement experiences can build confidence and participation over time.

slides.title: Try This Today
slides.content: Notice one situation that increases concern and one thing that helps you feel more capable. You will use these observations later this week.
